decisions.reason: A separate same-message MODIFY already captures the 4–6 complete systems, E/L as the primary variable, distinct architectural philosophies, and removal of the prior preferred direction. The kerning exploration adds no further E/L state change.
The instruction that the approved Hero V remain unchanged reaffirms its existing fixed-reference state and does not modify its geometry requirement.
Preserving the previously defined subtle second-V hierarchy reaffirms the candidate's existing height and visual-role attributes without changing them.
The source requests multiple complete concepts and limited spacing exploration but does not change the obligation to explain design intentions or their translation into rendered forms.
The source preserves the literal accent derivation but does not alter the existing exact peak-alignment rule or its fixed Hero V reference.
The source preserves the second V's established hierarchy but does not change its derivation, signature reach, or other glyph geometry.
Requiring the É accent to remain a literal copy of the Hero V termination reaffirms the existing shared-terminal rule and introduces no new terminal treatment.
The source explicitly preserves the already-established literal copy relationship; it does not change the accent's derivation source, vector-match requirement, or redrawing prohibition.
The source concerns black-and-white wordmark concept structure and spacing and does not resume or otherwise modify the deferred champagne material treatment.
